paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: who you listen to shapes where you end up. The elders told Rehoboam, "If you will be a servant to these people and serve them this day, and if you will respond by speaking kind words to them, they will be your servants forever." (1 Kings 12:7) He had wise advice, free of charge, and he walked right past it (1 Kings 12:8). I think it's easy to pick the voice that sounds BIG over the voice that sounds wise, and that's a trap for all of us.

Now look at how the people were talking. They asked him to lighten the load, and they said they would serve him (1 Kings 12:4). Kindness was sitting right there, and Rehoboam answered "harshly" instead (1 Kings 12:13). A king who holds power tight can lose it fast, and a gentle answer could have kept a lot more together. So when someone comes to you with a heavy load, remember that how you answer them matters as much as what you answer.

But here's the part that makes me stop and just breathe. The writer says this turn of events "was from the LORD, to fulfill the word He had spoken to Jeroboam son of Nebat through Ahijah the Shilonite." (1 Kings 12:15) Even in a mess made by a stubborn king, God's word still stands. When the LORD says through Shemaiah, "for this is My doing," the warriors listen and turn back (1 Kings 12:24). That's the lesson I want you to carry, friend: listen to wise counsel, answer people gently, and when God speaks, turn around and obey.
